samples.original_name: SiC/FeCoCrNiCu/SiC joint obtained in air at 1200 ℃ for 1 min

evidence.quote: The joining of SiC using FeCoCrNiCu alloy was achieved in air at 1200 ℃ for 1 min, and the microstructure of the joint is shown in Fig. 7 (a).
The FeCoCrNiCu high-entropy alloy was prepared by the arc-melting method with a thickness of 100 µ m
The furnace temperature rose to 400 ℃ at a rate of 10 ℃ /min and held for 2 min.

The DC power supply was subsequently activated, and a constant voltage of 150 V was applied to the sample until the sample conductivity was achieved. The sample was held at 12 A-0.4 MPa for 1 s, 15 s, and 30 s, respectively.

The joining of SiC using FeCoCrNiCu alloy was achieved in air at 1200 ℃ for 1 min, and the microstructure of the joint is shown in Fig. 7 (a).
Fig. 7. (a) The backscattered electron image of the joint obtained in air at 1200 ℃ 1 min-0.4 MPa

In summary, the flash brazing of SiC is achieved using FeCoCrNiCu high-entropy alloy in air for seconds. The peak power density is 1.03 × 10^4 mW/mm^3, and the interface temperature instantaneously rises to 1570 ℃ at the moment of flash. During the stabilization period, the interfacial temperature ranges from 1080 ℃ to 1120 ℃, which ensures adequate interface reaction and element interdiffusion.
